Contentexpand_moreexpand_lessLearning objectives and content
    ObjectivesStudents are able to

Perform elementary calculations using the rules of probability theory
Work with discrete and continuous random variables and apply the important standard distributions in appropriate settings
Use joint distributions and properties when using multiple random variables such as independence and the Central Limit Theorem
Use discrete Markov chains and determine their properties and limiting distributions
Perform an exploratory data analysis of a data set
Identify properties of point estimators
Construct and interpret confidence intervals in various relevant settings
Apply hypothesis testing in various relevant settings and interpret the results
Explain how probability and statistics can be used in practice, for example in the analysis of random algorithms and real-world data sets

    ContentThis course gives an introduction to probability and statistics. Uncertainty shows up in many places within computer science. In complex systems you may need to consider failure rates of components, communication delays or imprecision in data or sensor input, whereas in algorithms randomness is used as a tool to create simpler or faster solutions. In these situations considering only best and worst-case behavior leads a an overly optimistic or pessimistic representation. Instead, a better option is often to model this uncertainty and analyze the model. Probability theory gives us the tools to do this and get a more accurate representation of the behavior of complex systems or algorithms. Statistics, on the other hand, concerns what can be learned from data. In this course you will learn how to build probabilistic models, perform statistical analyses of real data, and the theory behind all this.

Mastery of the course content is broken down to mastery of 14 course competencies. Each course competency is tested at 4 occasions (2 weekly tests, exam and resit). To pass the course, mastery of a sufficiently high number of course competencies needs to be demonstrated, and the more competencies are passed, the higher the grade. Additionally, there is a minimal requirement for the exam.
